title: Heaviest K Keeping Their Order
statement:
You get an array nums and an integer k. Choose exactly k elements so that their sum is as large as possible, and return them in the order they appear in nums.

If several choices give the same largest sum, any of them is accepted.

examples.why: The three largest values are 7, 7 and 4. They are returned in array order, not sorted.
All values are negative; drop the smallest one, -5, and keep the rest in order.
Either 2 can join the 9, so [9, 2] is also accepted.

hints: Forget the order for a moment. Which k values give the largest sum?
The k largest values. But you must return them in their original positions, so remember where each one came from.
Sort indices by value (or keep a min-heap of size k), take the top k indices, sort those indices, and read the values back.

explain.intuition:
The sum only depends on which elements you pick, so pick the k largest. The order requirement is a separate, easy step: once you know which positions you picked, sort the positions and read the values in that order.

The common mistake is to sort the values themselves, which loses the positions. Work with indices instead. A min-heap of size k also works: push each index, and when the heap grows past k, drop the index with the smallest value. What remains are the k best positions.
steps: Create the list of indices 0 … n−1.
Sort the indices by nums[i], largest first, and keep the first k.
Sort those k indices in increasing order.
pitfalls: Returning the k largest values in sorted order, like [7, 7, 4] instead of [4, 7, 7].
Picking every element equal to the k-th largest value. With ties, that can give more than k elements.

complexity.time: O(n log n), or O(n log k) with a heap

solutions.title: Drop the smallest, one at a time
solutions.idea: Remove the smallest remaining element n − k times. What is left is the answer, already in order.

solutions.title: Sort indices
solutions.idea: Sort positions by value, keep the best k positions, then put those positions back in order.

solutions.title: Min-heap of size k
solutions.idea: Stream indices into a heap keyed by value. Whenever it holds more than k, pop the smallest. Sort the survivors by index.

followups: Do it in O(n) average time with quickselect. How do you handle ties at the k-th value?
The elements must also be contiguous. Which technique applies now?
lcTitle: Find Subsequence of Length K With the Largest Sum
